activity_context.topic_title: Solving Decoupled Homogeneous Systems of ODEs

feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2){x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{2}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$
